findings.evidence: The divergent-remote branch says to run `git cherry "$orig" "$remote"` and, "if every line starts with `-` ... continue and push with the lease on `$remote`". Git cherry excludes merge commits. A remote-only merge can contain unique conflict-resolution changes even when every non-merge commit has a patch-equivalent local commit. This branch permits the subsequent force-push to discard those changes; the explicit lease only verifies that the remote tip has not moved.
findings.fix: Before accepting the all-minus result, check `git rev-list --merges "$orig..$remote"`. If that range contains merges, stop, list them and require reconciliation rather than treating git cherry as proof that all remote changes are preserved. Restrict the patch-equivalence fast path to a remote-only range without merge commits.
